claims.text: Local chemical short-range order governs phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Selective negative mixing enthalpies occur between particular element pairs, including Al–Ni and Cr–Fe.
Chemical short-range order stabilizes a single-phase microstructure.
Chemical short-range order suppresses the formation of deleterious intermetallic precipitates.
Rapid quenching after solution treatment typically produces a single-phase Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy with minimal enforced short-range order.
Controlled variation of annealing temperature and hold time can systematically vary the degree of short-range order while composition remains constant.
Moderate-temperature annealing around 800°C promotes atomic diffusivity and short-range ordering.
Slow cooling after annealing allows further development of short-range order.
The magnitude and spatial extent of local chemical short-range order can be characterized using diffuse X-ray or neutron scattering or atom-probe tomography.
Negative pairwise mixing enthalpies drive localized chemical ordering.
Short-range order reduces the thermodynamic driving force for intermetallic-phase nucleation.
Reducing the driving force for intermetallic nucleation stabilizes a single-phase structure.
Heat-treated samples with enhanced short-range order will exhibit delayed or suppressed intermetallic precipitation relative to rapidly quenched baseline samples.
Samples with enhanced short-range order will retain higher high-temperature strength than the baseline alloy.
Samples with enhanced short-range order will show superior radiation tolerance relative to the baseline alloy.
Samples with enhanced short-range order will maintain greater cryogenic toughness than the baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism operates where atomic mobility permits short-range ordering but below the temperature at which complete equilibrium phase separation occurs.
The hypothesis is limited to the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni compositions under investigation and may not transfer to substantially different compositions or phase diagrams.
Grain size and residual stress could influence the measured performance independently of short-range order.
